content.theory:
Forms collect input from users — signups, logins, searches. A form is built from three things: the `<form>` wrapper, `<input>` fields, and a submit `<button>`.

### The form element
```html
<form action="/api/register" method="post">
  ...fields...
</form>
```

- `action` = where the data is sent
- `method` = `get` or `post`

### Text input
The workhorse field:
```html
<input type="text" name="username" placeholder="Pick a username">
```
- `name` = the key the server receives (required!)
- `placeholder` = grey hint text

### Labels
Always pair inputs with `<label>` for accessibility — clicking the label focuses the field:
```html
<label for="username">Username</label>
<input type="text" id="username" name="username">
```
The `for` attribute must match the input's `id`.

### Common input types
| Type | Use |
|------|-----|
| `text` | Single line of text |
| `email` | Email address (browser validates format) |
| `password` | Masked text |
| `number` | Numeric value |
| `date` | Date picker |

### Textarea & submit
```html
<textarea name="message" rows="4"></textarea>
<button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
```

exercise.instruction: Create a form with a text input for a username. Give it a label 'Username', an id of 'username', and a name of 'username'. Add a submit button labelled 'Sign In'.
